questions.q: Propene is treated first with B₂H₆ in THF and then with H₂O₂/NaOH. The major organic product is:
questions.explain: Boron adds to the terminal CH₂ and is later replaced by OH, so water is added anti-Markovnikov to give propan-1-ol. Propan-2-ol is the acid-catalysed hydration (and oxymercuration) product.

questions.q: Which statement about hydroboration–oxidation of an alkene is NOT correct?
options: A carbocation intermediate forms, so hydride shifts can occur
B and H add to the same face of the alkene
Boron attaches to the less substituted carbon
The alkyl group moves from boron to oxygen with retention of configuration
questions.explain: BH₃ adds through a concerted four-centred transition state with no carbocation, so there is no rearrangement. The other three statements are the key features of the reaction.

questions.q: Tripropylborane, (CH₃CH₂CH₂)₃B, obtained from propene, is to be converted into propan-1-amine. The correct reagent is:
questions.explain: Chloramine (or hydroxylamine-O-sulfonic acid) aminates the trialkylborane to propan-1-amine. Ammonia alone is the common trap; H₂O₂/NaOH gives the alcohol and a carboxylic acid gives propane by protonolysis.

questions.q: 1-Methylcyclopentene is subjected to hydroboration–oxidation (BH₃·THF, then H₂O₂/NaOH). The product is:
questions.explain: OH goes to the less substituted ring carbon, and H and OH add syn (cis to each other), which leaves the methyl group and OH trans. 1-Methylcyclopentan-1-ol would be the Markovnikov product.
